point: The section reviews research on investment and operational decisions in power systems affected by stochastic renewables.
High renewable shares raise the need for flexibility, but studies disagree on whether storage or transmission is the best provider.
Power system optimisation models are split into capacity expansion models for investments and operational models for markets.
Studies of operational multi-market models show renewable forecast errors affect costs, prices, reserves and market design.
Capacity expansion studies show stochastic treatment of renewables changes investments, raising system cost and favouring flexible providers.
Combining investment with market sequencing shows forecast errors matter, though the existing model was small, so market sequencing should shape results.
This thesis fills the gap of capacity expansion with market sequencing in larger systems with transmission and storage.
